tasks.name: Use and differentiate resource and data blocks
Refer to resource attributes and create cross-resource references
Write dynamic configuration using expressions and functions
Understand best practices for managing sensitive data, including secrets management with Vault

concepts.name: Resources and data sources
concepts.description: resource manages objects; data reads existing information.

concepts.name: References and dependency graph
concepts.description: References carry values and create implicit graph dependencies.

concepts.name: Input variables
concepts.description: Variables parameterize configurations and can define type, validation, sensitivity, and ephemerality.

concepts.name: Outputs
concepts.description: Outputs expose values from a module or root configuration.

concepts.name: Terraform types
concepts.description: Terraform supports primitive and complex collection/structural types.

concepts.name: Expressions and functions
concepts.description: Expressions transform values; functions include can, try, merge, flatten, json/yaml encoders and decoders.

concepts.name: count and for_each
concepts.description: count uses numeric indexes; for_each uses stable map/set keys known before apply.

concepts.name: depends_on
concepts.description: Explicit hidden dependency used when no value reference expresses the real dependency.

concepts.name: Lifecycle rules
concepts.description: Lifecycle controls replacement order, destroy protection, ignored updates, and replacement triggers.

concepts.name: Custom conditions
concepts.description: Variable validation, preconditions, postconditions, and check blocks validate different stages.

concepts.name: Sensitive values
concepts.description: Sensitive marks redact normal display but can still persist in plan/state.

concepts.name: Ephemeral and write-only values
concepts.description: Ephemeral values and provider write-only arguments avoid persistence in Terraform artifacts where supported.

concepts.name: YAML with Terraform
concepts.description: yamlencode and yamldecode bridge Terraform values with YAML documents.

concepts.name: Vault-backed secrets
concepts.description: Vault can provide centrally managed or dynamic secrets to Terraform, but secret persistence still depends on how Terraform consumes and stores the values.

questions.prompt: Place the secret-handling mechanisms by normal-display redaction and persistence in plan/state.

items.label: sensitive = true

questions.explanation: `sensitive` redacts normal display but can still persist. Combining sensitive + ephemeral both redacts and prevents persistence in plan/state in supported ephemeral contexts; ordinary values are visible and persisted when tracked.

questions.prompt: Classify the statements about using Vault with Terraform.

items.label: Vault can be a source of centrally managed or dynamic credentials/secrets.
Reading a secret from Vault automatically guarantees that Terraform will never persist the value in state or plan files.
You must still consider sensitive, ephemeral, and write-only handling after the secret enters Terraform data flow.

questions.explanation: Vault improves secret issuance and retrieval, but it does not by itself change Terraform artifact semantics. A value read into a normal persisted attribute can still appear in state; use supported ephemeral/write-only flows when omission from Terraform artifacts is required.
hints: Separate secret source from secret persistence: Vault answers where the secret comes from; Terraform language/provider features answer whether it is stored.

questions.prompt: An instance should be replaced whenever a managed launch-template version changes, even if the instance arguments themselves do not force replacement. Choose the lifecycle design.

steps.prompt: Which lifecycle feature models this dependency?

choices.label: replace_triggered_by referencing the managed launch template/version
Arbitrary locals and plain variables directly

questions.explanation: `replace_triggered_by` watches managed resources/attributes. If a plain value must drive replacement, model that value through a managed `terraform_data` resource rather than expecting arbitrary locals to work directly.

steps.prompt: Why is the companion version argument useful?

choices.label: Terraform cannot diff the write-only secret, so an explicit version/change signal tells the provider when to resend/update
It encrypts the password in state
It stores a hash for Terraform to compare

questions.explanation: Ephemeral values are omitted from Terraform artifacts, and write-only arguments let a provider consume a value without returning it to Terraform for persistence. Because Terraform cannot compare a write-only value later, providers commonly expose an explicit version/change argument.
